back: Patchify, linear projection to width $D$, prepend class token, add positional embedding, $L$ pre-norm transformer blocks, head on the class token.
$N=(H/p)(W/p)$; each patch has $Cp^2$ values. $224$ and $p=16$ give $196$ (197 tokens with the class token).
A conv with kernel $p$, stride $p$ and $D$ output channels equals the linear projection of each flattened patch.
Smaller patches: more tokens, finer detail, attention cost $\propto(N+1)^2$ (halving $p$ multiplies it by 16). Larger: faster, coarser.
Learned vector prepended to the sequence; its final state is the global image representation fed to the classifier.
CNN: locality and translation equivariance built in. ViT: learned, so it needs more data or stronger recipes (DeiT augmentation, pre-training).
Heavy augmentation (RandAugment, mixup, CutMix, random erasing), stochastic depth, repeated augmentation, optional distillation from a CNN.
Contrastive (SimCLR, MoCo, CLIP), teacher-student (DINO, BYOL), masked reconstruction (MAE, BEiT).
$\ell_i=-\log\frac{\exp(s_{i,i^+}/\tau)}{\sum_{k\ne i}\exp(s_{ik}/\tau)}$ with cosine similarity $s$, averaged over all $2N$ views.
$\log(2N-1)$ when every similarity is equal (a $(2N-1)$-way guess).
Small $\tau$ sharpens the softmax and emphasises hard negatives; large $\tau$ weighs all negatives alike.
More negatives per anchor make the task harder and more informative; MoCo uses a queue of past embeddings instead.
Student matches an EMA teacher on another view; centring and sharpening of the teacher output prevent collapse; no negatives.
Mask about 75% of patches, encode the visible ones, small decoder reconstructs masked pixels (MSE on masked patches); discard the decoder after pre-training.
Freeze the encoder, train one linear classifier on labels, report top-1; a clean measure of feature quality.
